query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A genuine categorical axis for grouping crew experiences, useful for the exploratory query. However groundedness is undermined: row 2 mentions nothing about crew yet was labelled 'rude_dismissive', an invented negative that contradicts the silence of the text; a NULL/not-stated would have been correct. Other samples are well-read.

per_column.name: seat_hardware_condition
per_column.rationale: Useful new axis on physical cabin condition with a sensible NULL for silent rows. But row 2 describes seats as 'dreadful'/'poor padding' yet was labelled 'adequate_functional', contradicting the text; row 1's 'new_excellent' is a stretch from 'well sanitized'. Mixed grounding.

per_column.name: food_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: Distinct, groupable food dimension with appropriate NULLs. However row 2 says nothing about food but was labelled 'poor_inedible', an invented value; text-supported rows are read well.

per_column.name: special_meal_handling
per_column.rationale: Highly skewed boolean (832/68) with limited analytical leverage for a general 'what's worth analyzing' query. The False values in samples are consistent with texts that don't mention special meals, so grounding is reasonable.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: A meaningful axis distinguishing how disruptions were handled, with a dominant 'no_disruption' default that correctly reflects silent rows. Sample labels align with texts.

per_column.name: service_decline_signal
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean flag that largely restates negative crew/service signal already captured by crew_service_quality; limited independent leverage. Sample values (all False) are consistent with the texts.

per_column.name: premium_economy_value_gap
per_column.rationale: Very rare True (50/900) boolean of narrow scope; low leverage for a broad exploratory query. It also presumes a premium-economy value judgment often not stated; defaulting to False is defensible but the concept is weakly supported by most texts.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely useful categorical axes (crew, seat, food, disruption handling) that let the analyst group and compare aspects, directly serving the 'which aspect is worth analyzing' query; a few booleans (special_meal, service_decline, premium_economy_gap) are skewed or redundant and add little. Groundedness is moderate: silent-row NULLs and defaults are handled well, but the aspect-categorization columns show a recurring failure on row 2, where crew, seat, and food were assigned confident (and even contradicting) values despite the text supporting only the seat complaint — indicating over-eager labelling of unmentioned aspects.
